candidate.blueprint_locator: Safe and Effective Care Environment — Management of Care: understand legal/regulatory requirements and coordinate care with public-health systems when communicable-disease control measures apply.
candidate.blueprint_topic: Management of Care — legal/public-health distinction between quarantine and isolation
candidate.educational_objective: Distinguish quarantine, which applies to people exposed to a contagious disease who may become ill, from isolation, which separates people who are sick with a communicable disease from those who are not sick, while recognizing that legal authority varies by jurisdiction.

options.A: Quarantine separates or restricts movement of people who were exposed to a contagious disease to see whether they become ill; isolation separates people who are sick with a quarantinable communicable disease from people who are not sick.
options.B: Quarantine and isolation are legally identical terms that apply only to people with confirmed symptomatic infection.
options.C: Quarantine applies only after laboratory confirmation of infection, whereas isolation is used for people who were merely exposed.
options.D: Quarantine has no public-health legal basis in the United States and can be used only as an informal voluntary suggestion.

candidate.rationale: A is correct. CDC's current legal-authorities guidance defines quarantine as separating and restricting movement of people exposed to a contagious disease to determine whether they become sick, whereas isolation separates sick people with a quarantinable communicable disease from people who are not sick. B and C reverse or collapse the two concepts. D is incorrect because isolation and quarantine have established state and federal legal authorities; however, the exact legal authority and procedures depend on jurisdiction and circumstance.
candidate.source_claim_supported: CDC distinguishes quarantine as restriction of exposed persons who may become ill from isolation of sick persons; both have established public-health legal foundations, with implementation depending on applicable authority.
candidate.source_document_title: Legal Authorities for Isolation and Quarantine; Laws and Regulations Governing the Control of Communicable Diseases
candidate.source_locator: Legal Authorities for Isolation and Quarantine — Isolation and Quarantine: isolation separates sick people with a quarantinable communicable disease from people who are not sick; quarantine separates and restricts movement of people exposed to a contagious disease to see if they become sick. The page also describes isolation/quarantine as police-power functions. Laws and Regulations Governing the Control of Communicable Diseases — federal authority is implemented under Title 42 and relevant regulations, while state/local authorities also exist.
